free.title: BRIC Celebrate Brooklyn! - Common
free.caption:
Common is playing Prospect Park this Friday, and it costs nothing.

BRIC Celebrate Brooklyn! is the longest-running free outdoor arts festival in New York, and this year's Harry Belafonte night is the one to save. Common headlines, Adi Oasis opens, and the two 2026 Action Lab Belafonte Fellows get named live from the Lena Horne Bandshell stage. The bandshell holds more than 8,000 people in Park Slope, but nothing is reserved - the ones who turn up early are the ones who see it properly.

Tip: gates open at 6, a full hour before the music. Bring a blanket, a sealed plastic bottle and dinner from Fifth Ave. Cans and glass get turned away at the gate.

📷 BRIC

food.title: Japan Village Summer Festival
food.caption:
Free entry, a noodle-eating contest, and a round-trip ticket to Japan on the line.

The Japan Village Summer Festival takes over Industry City in Sunset Park, Brooklyn on Saturday - the sixth year the Japanese food hall has thrown this thing, and it still costs nothing to walk in. Folk dance troupes run through Yosakoi, Hanagasa Ondo and Awa Odori, taiko drummers take the afternoon, and there is a watermelon-splitting contest at 2:50 for anyone who thinks summer peaked in July. Close to 8,000 people turned up last year.

Tip: the food hall opens at 11, two hours before the ceremony. Eat then, watch after.

📷 Japan Village

art.title: Blooming Wonders at ARTECHOUSE
art.caption:
There is a digital flower garden under Chelsea Market, and it closes September 14.

Blooming Wonders is ARTECHOUSE NYC's own production, staged in a 100-year-old boiler room beneath the market in Chelsea. Projected blossoms run floor to ceiling, a milkweed bloom releases a swarm of monarchs the second you walk toward it, and two walls turn into instruments you can play with your hands. SUBMERGE, a twelve-artist digital showcase, is running in the same space on the same ticket. Three weeks left on both.

Tip: weekday afternoons are the quiet slots. Weekends and anything after 5PM sell out first.

📷 ARTECHOUSE
